subject: browser-credential-boundary
seam: crates/api/src/credential_boundary.rs (new: render_operator_record + check_boot); crates/api/src/main.rs:204-215 (boot gate before the store, the router and the bind); crates/api/src/billing.rs:37-56 (first live emitter: the rejected-webhook operator record)
seam_notes: Both halves landed as the technique states them. Boot gate: AuthMode::Enforced starts; unenforced starts ONLY with LIGHTTRACK_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED set to a full sentence; otherwise anyhow::bail naming both remedies. It reads the admin key by VALUE, not presence — a blank LIGHTTRACK_ADMIN_KEY does not change the verdict, only the diagnosis, since under Dev any/no token resolves to Principal::Dev and the key gates nothing. Allowlist: six named fields survive, every header is rendered by name with its value replaced (headers as a category, never a list), every unanticipated field is dropped, values capped at 256 chars on a char boundary. Wired live at the one seam that already reads credential-bearing headers — billing webhook signature failure — so the pass observes emitted bytes rather than an intention. cargo check -p lighttrack-api clean; cargo test -p lighttrack-api 223 passed / 0 failed (219 before, +4 new); clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.
falsifier: The proposal's own falsifier — 'if every tracklight instance is bound to loopback the banner is already sufficient' — was checked before writing code and is FALSE: deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml:14-18 and deploy/docker/Dockerfile:34-39 both bind 0.0.0.0 with LIGHTTRACK_AUTH_MODE defaulting to dev, and deploy/helm values.yaml:16 binds 0.0.0.0 too. So the shipped artifacts are the reachable-and-unauthenticated configuration, not a hypothetical one. Remaining live falsifier: if LIGHTTRACK_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED ever appears in deploy/ or the README quickstart, the gate has been converted into a default and should be reverted rather than tuned. Second falsifier, untested here: the allowlist has exactly one emitter, so 'the allowlist collides with debuggability' cannot be observed yet — it becomes falsifiable when the pass is put over crates/api/src/logging.rs's ingest fields.

subject: retry-backoff
seam: crates/engine/src/retry.rs (with_retry_within: stated delay outranks the computed rung, CALL_BUDGET deadline, over-budget terminal state)
crates/engine/src/providers.rs (stated_retry_after: 3 header spellings / 2 unit systems, classified at the boundary)
crates/runner/src/compare.rs (TargetHealth: one breaker per target as a candidate filter, all-open degrades to trying)
seam_notes: The direction said with_retry's CLOSURE signature must widen so the response reaches the scheduler; it does not have to. The response is gone by then, but the CLASS is not: putting the stated delay on EngineError::RateLimited keeps classification at the boundary that holds the structured response and leaves the FnMut() -> Result<T> seam and all 4 call sites untouched. The health filter had to live in compute_cell, not beside it: compare dispatches ONE parallel_map over target x case, so a filter over a pre-computed candidate list has nothing to filter - the verdict is consulted per cell, target-major, and identity is the pre-filter index. Provider-boundary suite is a ~40-line std::net::TcpListener stub, not wiremock/httpmock/mockito: the engine client is BLOCKING reqwest and all three are async, so each would drag a tokio runtime plus a cargo-deny surface into a crate that has neither, to serve one canned response.
falsifier: The retry-after half rests on providers actually stating a delay on 429. This run could not check it - the worktree carries no engine log corpus - so it remains the proposal's own open falsifier: if a week of crates/engine logs shows no Retry-After on any 429 received, the header accept-list is dead code and only the 60s CALL_BUDGET deadline is earning its keep. The filter's falsifier is cheaper: if run history shows errored_cases at zero across every recorded run, the breaker guards a case that has not occurred.
